answer: Each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before admission; because every result depends on the previous one, GPUs cannot parallelize a single chain to remove its elapsed-time cost. An attacker may run clones concurrently, but each clone still requires its own completed proof, limiting rapid Sybil creation. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the work cheaply, while the canyon of required delay sets a clear horizon for admission and prevents nectar-sweet shortcuts.
